scenarios.desc: PR metadata check request using documented trigger phrases
scenarios.input:
Here is my PR title and body. Title: `added the retry thing`. Body: `## Summary

Makes the uploader retry.

## Changes

- retry loop

## Type of Change

- [ ] Bug fix`. Validate my PR description before I submit it. Answer in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: The prompt uses the documented trigger `validate my PR description` without naming the skill, and supplies input that fails all three checks: the title has no conventional-commit type, the body carries no issue-linking keyword, and the Type of Change checkbox is unmarked. A response that reports the three failures separately, names the missing type prefix, and names a linking keyword is attributable to this skill rather than to generic PR advice.

scenarios.desc: Closing-keyword recommendation must be checked against the diff
scenarios.input: My PR title is `fix(auth): stop the session cookie expiring early` and the body says `Refs #412`. Issue #412 asks for the whole session-refresh rewrite; this PR only changes one expiry constant. Check my PR title and body. Answer in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: The title and keyword are both well-formed, so a checker reading format alone reports a clean pass and recommends upgrading `Refs` to `Closes`. The skill's Phase 3 requires verifying a closing keyword against the diff first. A response that keeps `Refs #412` because the diff does not deliver what the issue asks is attributable to the skill; one that recommends `Closes #412` on format grounds is not.

scenarios.desc: Code review request stays outside PR metadata validation
scenarios.input: Review the retry loop in uploader.py for correctness and race conditions. Answer in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: This asks for a code review of a diff, which the skill's description explicitly routes elsewhere. It names no PR title, no PR body, and no metadata trigger phrase, so validate-pr-description should stay inactive.
